rows.text: Every step of it fell on ground the map had never held.
{newPerHundred:Words} paces in a hundred fell on roads that had never felt your step.
A sliver of fresh ground at the edge of the old, and the map took it gladly.
Fresh ground, and the map is wider for it.
The fog gave a little more back today, and it keeps nothing it has given.
A thousand cells of the map are yours now, and not one of them will fog again.
Five thousand cells of the map are yours now, and not one of them will fog again.
Ten thousand cells of the map are yours now, and not one of them will fog again.
Twenty-five thousand cells of the map are yours now, and not one of them will fog again.
Fifty thousand cells of the map are yours now, and not one of them will fog again.
A hundred thousand cells of the map are yours now, and not one of them will fog again.
Ground you had let rest for half a year woke under your feet.
You returned to {street} after {rearmGapDays:words} days. It remembered you.
rows.note: Street from the basemap's roads layer, gap from each re-armed cell's stored previous lastRunAt (0256, D-302). Runs classified before 0256 wait until their reveal set is rewritten.

rows.text: {soonStreet} comes back into season in {rearmInDays:words} days.
rows.note: THE ONLY FORWARD-LOOKING LINE (§3.5 rule 4). An invitation, never a deadline; a second forward-looking row needs a decision record. The nearby cell (within 4 rings, ~170 m) that re-arms soonest as of the run, from the classes object (0262); soonStreet, not street, because a run can return to one street and pass near another.

rows.text: The longest road in all the record.
The longest road you have walked in a year.
The {roadCount:ordinal} road in the record, and every one of them still on the map.
You have now walked fifty leagues. The record holds every one.
You have now walked a hundred leagues. The record holds every one.
You have now walked two hundred and fifty leagues. The record holds every one.
You have now walked five hundred leagues. The record holds every one.
You have now walked a thousand leagues. The record holds every one.
Old roads, run well. The map holds them still.
These roads know your weight by now, and they were glad of it.
Another line laid down in the web of your roads. It darkens where you return.
Work the map cannot see, and the record keeps it all the same.
Set down in the record, where nothing is ever lost.
